visual_logic: Highlights the robust, flat, pearl-like crushing teeth located behind the toothless beak tip of Noripterus.
prompt: High-fidelity 3D asset of a rear jaw profile from a Noripterus, showcase-focused on its unique 'Shell Crushing Peg' teeth, rendered in a 3D animated feature film aesthetic with soft, stylized edges. The bone gives way to robust, thick, flat, button-like crushing teeth clustered heavily at the rear, resembling heavily worn smooth ivory molars. The texture of the bone matches a pale tan and yellowish-grey calcified fossil finish. The specimen is oriented diagonally and perfectly centered in a 1:1 square composition, carefully scaled to occupy the central power-zone, ensuring a strict 25% negative space safety margin on all four sides. Placed flat against a neutral, 50% grey studio floor plane with high-contrast contact shadows. Illuminated by soft studio lighting with ambient occlusion to accentuate the thick, flat, heavy pressure surfaces of the teeth.
